items.label: f02-atomic-vs-stale
items.front: Atomic replacement and stale-write detection solve different problems. What does each one prevent?
items.back: Writing a complete temporary file and atomically moving it over the target means a reader never sees half a snapshot. It does not show whether the candidate was built from an old read; detecting that needs a comparison against what this session loaded, done under a lock.

items.label: f03-lock-file
items.front: What is the tasks.txt.lock file next to the data file for?
items.back: It is the object the cooperative file lock is taken on during a save, so participating processes take turns. The app keeps it on disk; do not delete it while sessions are running. Programs that ignore the lock are not protected by it.

items.label: f01-immutable-task
items.front: Why is Task immutable, and what does an edit return?
items.back: If a manager hands out mutable tasks, a caller can change them without validation or saving. Task has only final fields; edit and withCompletion build a new Task instead of changing the old one, and the constructor re-runs all validation. The service decides whether that replacement becomes accepted state.

items.prompt: A file in the original key=value format holds two complete tasks with ids 2 and 5. The user starts the app and adds a task. Which id does it get?

choices.text: Id 3, which is the first free gap after the lowest legacy id
Id 3, as it is the number of tasks plus one
Id 1, as a converted file then starts a completely fresh count
Id 6, one above the highest legacy id that was loaded

choices: Id 3, which is the first free gap after the lowest legacy id
Id 3, as it is the number of tasks plus one
Id 1, as a converted file then starts a completely fresh count
Id 6, one above the highest legacy id that was loaded

items.explanation: The legacy format has no watermark, so legacy() computes next = max(id) + 1 = 6 and builds the snapshot with it (reproduced: "Task 6 added and saved."). From then on the TODOLIST1 header keeps the watermark.

items.prompt: A task is added (version 1), edited once, completed with option 3, then reopened with option 7. How does option 2 show it?

choices.text: [ ] ID 1 / v4 with the old Completed time still listed below it
[X] ID 1 / v4, as option 7 keeps the task marked as completed
[ ] ID 1 / v4 with no Completed line, as reopening clears it
[ ] ID 1 / v2, as completing and reopening do not count as edits

choices: [ ] ID 1 / v4 with the old Completed time still listed below it
[X] ID 1 / v4, as option 7 keeps the task marked as completed
[ ] ID 1 / v4 with no Completed line, as reopening clears it
[ ] ID 1 / v2, as completing and reopening do not count as edits

items.explanation: edit and each real withCompletion change build a new Task with nextVersion(), so add, edit, complete and reopen give versions 1 to 4. Reopening passes null as completedAt, and the display adds a Completed line only for completed tasks (reproduced: "[ ] ID 1 / v4 - X2").

items.prompt: Option 6 reads task 1 with selected() and passes its getVersion() straight to editTask in the same command. When can that call fail with "Task version changed"?

choices.text: When task 1 was completed or reopened earlier in this same session
Never from the menu, since the version was just read from the same snapshot
When option 9 has reloaded the file since this session's previous edit
When another terminal saved an edit to task 1 after this session loaded

choices: When task 1 was completed or reopened earlier in this same session
Never from the menu, since the version was just read from the same snapshot
When option 9 has reloaded the file since this session's previous edit
When another terminal saved an edit to task 1 after this session loaded

items.explanation: expected() compares the version passed in with the task in the manager's snapshot, and option 6 read that version from the same snapshot moments earlier on one thread, so they always match. Another terminal's save does not change this session's snapshot; that conflict is caught later by the baseline comparison in save. Completing, reopening and reloading all update the snapshot before selected() reads it.

items.prompt: A valid TODOLIST1 tasks file is saved again by an editor that turns every line ending into CRLF. What happens at the next start?

choices.text: Startup stops with a legacy-field error, and the file is left untouched
The CR characters are stripped on load, and the tasks open as normal
It starts with no tasks, and the next save writes a fresh TODOLIST1 file
Startup stops with "Truncated snapshot." because of the extra characters

choices: Startup stops with a legacy-field error, and the file is left untouched
The CR characters are stripped on load, and the tasks open as normal
It starts with no tasks, and the next save writes a fresh TODOLIST1 file
Startup stops with "Truncated snapshot." because of the extra characters

items.explanation: decode takes the TODOLIST1 branch only when the text starts with TODOLIST1 followed by a bare line feed. With CRLF it falls through to legacy(), which rejects the TODOLIST1 line as a field without '='. main prints "Startup stopped; existing data was not replaced. Unknown, duplicate or malformed legacy field." and exits with code 1 (reproduced). Nothing strips CR characters, and a failed load never becomes an empty list.

items.prompt: A user adds A (id 1) and B (id 2), deletes B, exits, restarts the app and adds C. Which id does C get?

choices.text: Id 1, as numbering starts again after every restart
Id 2, as deleted ids are put back into a free list
Id 3, from the next-id watermark saved in the file header
Id 2, from the highest surviving id plus one at the restart

choices: Id 1, as numbering starts again after every restart
Id 2, as deleted ids are put back into a free list
Id 3, from the next-id watermark saved in the file header
Id 2, from the highest surviving id plus one at the restart

items.explanation: addTask takes the id from snapshot.nextId(), and encode writes that watermark on the header line next to the revision. Deleting B leaves the watermark at 3, so C is "Task 3 added and saved." (reproduced). Nothing recomputes it from the surviving ids or keeps a free list.

items.prompt: The app is started with a file name that does not exist yet. The user lists tasks and chooses 5. What is on disk afterwards?

choices.text: A lock file and an empty task file next to each other
An empty TODOLIST1 file, written out when the session ends
An empty TODOLIST1 file, written as soon as it loads
Nothing; the file is first written by an accepted change

choices: A lock file and an empty task file next to each other
An empty TODOLIST1 file, written out when the session ends
An empty TODOLIST1 file, written as soon as it loads
Nothing; the file is first written by an accepted change

items.explanation: bytes() returns null for a missing file and load() treats that as an empty snapshot without writing. Only save writes, and only a mutation calls it; listing and exiting never do (reproduced: no file existed afterwards; the unit test "missing file loads without creating data" checks the same).

items.prompt: A user picks 1 and types a title, and then the input ends before the description is entered. What happens?

choices.text: It crashes with a NoSuchElementException and a full stack trace
The task is kept in memory, and saved by the exit code afterwards too
The task is added with an empty description, and then the app exits
It reports the command was not applied, and the file is unchanged

choices: It crashes with a NoSuchElementException and a full stack trace
The task is kept in memory, and saved by the exit code afterwards too
The task is added with an empty description, and then the app exits
It reports the command was not applied, and the file is unchanged

items.explanation: line() throws NoSuchElementException when there is no next line, so addTask is never called. run() catches it and prints "Input ended; incomplete command was not applied." and the finally block only closes the scanner (reproduced: the file bytes were identical before and after).

items.prompt: An add fails inside save because the atomic move throws. What do the file and the manager hold afterwards?

choices.text: The old file bytes, but the manager lists the new task too
A partly written file that the next start then cannot parse
The new file, but the manager still lists the old tasks
The old file bytes, and only the tasks accepted before it

choices: The old file bytes, but the manager lists the new task too
A partly written file that the next start then cannot parse
The new file, but the manager still lists the old tasks
The old file bytes, and only the tasks accepted before it

items.explanation: commit calls repository.save first and assigns snapshot = candidate only after it returns; the temp file is deleted in finally and the target was never replaced. The test "atomic replacement failure retains memory and disk" checks both the bytes and getAllTasks (it passed when run).

items.prompt: After that refusal, session B chooses 9 (Reload) and enters its task again. What happens?

choices.text: It is accepted as task 2, and both tasks are listed
It is accepted as task 1, which replaces A's task
It is refused again until session A has been closed
It is accepted, but only B lists it until A reloads

choices: It is accepted as task 2, and both tasks are listed
It is accepted as task 1, which replaces A's task
It is refused again until session A has been closed
It is accepted, but only B lists it until A reloads

items.explanation: reload() replaces B's baseline and snapshot with the current file, which holds A's task and a watermark of 2. The new add builds revision 2 on top of that and the byte comparison now matches, so "Task 2 added and saved." and the list shows both (reproduced). The lock is only held during a save.

items.prompt: At "Status (all/open/done):" a user types Done with a capital D. What happens?

choices.text: It prints "Change not accepted: Invalid search or status."
It treats any status it does not know as all, and lists them
It asks again until one of the three lowercase words is typed
It lists the completed tasks whose text matches the search

choices: It prints "Change not accepted: Invalid search or status."
It treats any status it does not know as all, and lists them
It asks again until one of the three lowercase words is typed
It lists the completed tasks whose text matches the search

items.explanation: search checks List.of("all", "open", "done").contains(status), an exact, case-sensitive match, and throws IllegalArgumentException otherwise; the menu catch prints it (reproduced). The search text is lower-cased, but the status is not.

items.prompt: The tasks file exists but is empty (0 bytes). The user adds one task. Apart from the .lock file, what new file appears next to it?

choices.text: A .legacy-backup that holds a copy of the new TODOLIST1 snapshot
None, because an empty file holds no old data that needs a backup
A 0-byte .legacy-backup, as the empty file counts as old-format data
None; the add is refused, since an empty file cannot be decoded

choices: A .legacy-backup that holds a copy of the new TODOLIST1 snapshot
None, because an empty file holds no old data that needs a backup
A 0-byte .legacy-backup, as the empty file counts as old-format data
None; the add is refused, since an empty file cannot be decoded

items.explanation: legacy("") returns an empty snapshot, so the load succeeds with a non-null, zero-byte baseline. In save, that baseline does not start with TODOLIST1, so its bytes are written to <file>.legacy-backup before the new snapshot replaces the file (reproduced: the task file held the new snapshot and the backup was 0 bytes). The backup keeps the old bytes, not the new ones.

items.prompt: Task 1 is already completed. The user picks 3 and enters 1 again. What happens?

choices.text: It flips the task back to open, as option 3 toggles the state
It prints "Task state accepted." but no new version is saved
It saves version 3 with a fresh completion timestamp on it
It prints "Change not accepted:" as the task is already done

choices: It flips the task back to open, as option 3 toggles the state
It prints "Task state accepted." but no new version is saved
It saves version 3 with a fresh completion timestamp on it
It prints "Change not accepted:" as the task is already done

items.explanation: withCompletion returns the same object when the requested state equals the current one, and setCompleted returns early when replacement == old, so commit and save are skipped. App still prints its success line (reproduced: the file was byte-for-byte unchanged). Reopening is option 7.

items.prompt: Sessions A and B load the same empty file. A adds a task. B then tries to add a different task, is refused, and lists tasks. What does B show?

choices.text: B's own task only, as the add was applied before saving
A's task only, as the failed save re-read the current file
Both tasks, as B keeps its own task in memory as a draft
"No matching tasks.", as B still holds its old snapshot

choices: B's own task only, as the add was applied before saving
A's task only, as the failed save re-read the current file
Both tasks, as B keeps its own task in memory as a draft
"No matching tasks.", as B still holds its old snapshot

items.explanation: B's commit throws during save before snapshot = candidate, and nothing reloads automatically, so B keeps the empty snapshot it loaded. Listing an empty snapshot prints "No matching tasks." (reproduced with two JVMs). Only option 9 re-reads the file.

items.prompt: TaskRepository.save synchronizes on an object from the static LOCAL_LOCKS map before it calls channel.lock(). Why is that extra lock there?

choices.text: FileChannel.lock() only blocks other processes after a monitor is held
It stops other processes from writing the data file while the lock is held
It lets saves inside one JVM skip the slower file lock, which is only for speed
A second channel.lock() on the same file in one JVM throws instead of waiting

choices: FileChannel.lock() only blocks other processes after a monitor is held
It stops other processes from writing the data file while the lock is held
It lets saves inside one JVM skip the slower file lock, which is only for speed
A second channel.lock() on the same file in one JVM throws instead of waiting

items.explanation: File locks belong to the whole JVM: a second lock() on an overlapping region from the same JVM throws OverlappingFileLockException rather than blocking (reproduced with a two-channel test). The static map gives each lock path one monitor, so same-JVM callers such as two TaskManagers in the test suite wait their turn, and every save still takes the file lock. synchronized has no effect on other processes.

items.prompt: A user picks 4, enters task id 1, and at "Type DELETE:" types delete in lowercase. What happens?

choices.text: It deletes task 1, since the confirmation ignores case
It prints "Change not accepted:" and the reason for it
It prints "Deletion cancelled." and task 1 stays saved
It asks again until DELETE is typed in capital letters

choices: It deletes task 1, since the confirmation ignores case
It prints "Change not accepted:" and the reason for it
It prints "Deletion cancelled." and task 1 stays saved
It asks again until DELETE is typed in capital letters

items.explanation: App compares the stripped answer with equals("DELETE"), which is case-sensitive; any other text takes the else branch and prints "Deletion cancelled." without calling deleteTask (reproduced). There is no retry loop.

items.prompt: A user picks 6 for task 1 and presses Enter at both "New title:" and "New description:". What happens?

choices.text: Both fields are cleared, and the empty task is saved as v2
The edit is skipped, since nothing typed differs from before
The title is kept and only the description is cleared and saved
The edit is rejected for its title, and the file stays the same

choices: Both fields are cleared, and the empty task is saved as v2
The edit is skipped, since nothing typed differs from before
The title is kept and only the description is cleared and saved
The edit is rejected for its title, and the file stays the same

items.explanation: Task.edit builds a new Task, and its text() check requires 1..160 characters for the title, so a blank title throws IllegalArgumentException before commit. App prints "Change not accepted: Title must contain 1..160 characters without controls." (reproduced; the file was unchanged). A blank description alone is allowed and clears it.

items.prompt: The user picks 3 and, at "Task id:", types the eleven-digit number 99999999999. What does the app print?

choices.text: Change not accepted: Task not found.
A NumberFormatException stack trace, and then the app exits
Change not accepted: Enter a positive task id.
Change not accepted: For input string: "99999999999"

choices: Change not accepted: Task not found.
A NumberFormatException stack trace, and then the app exits
Change not accepted: Enter a positive task id.
Change not accepted: For input string: "99999999999"

items.explanation: selected() only checks the text against [1-9][0-9]*, which allows any number of digits, then calls Integer.parseInt, which throws NumberFormatException for a value above Integer.MAX_VALUE. NumberFormatException is a subclass of IllegalArgumentException, so the menu's catch prints its raw message (reproduced). The friendly id message is only for text the pattern rejects, and the lookup never runs.
